pages.text:
0.5 W Daya Bay Test Report 
1. Huizhou Daya Bay Video Link Range Test 
1.1 Test Objective 
To evaluate the 20 km video transmission performance of the in- house-
developed system in an air-to-ground scenario along the Daya Bay coastline. 
1.2 Test Environment 
Test date: May 14, 2026 
Test scenario: The test was conducted along the Huizhou Daya Bay coastline. 
The UAV was flown at an altitude of 80 m at one end of the link, while the ground 
station at the other end was mounted on a 1.8 m tripod. The target link distance 
was 20 km. 
Hardware: Four sets of in-house-developed 0.5 W equipment (two sets at each 
end: one test unit and one backup unit), two test laptops, six antennas, and one 
UAV test platform. 
Software: iPerf traffic -generation software, CRTdebug diagnostic software, 
and VLC media player. 
1.3 Test Results 
Test locations: 
UAV takeoff site: Wushantou Greenway Observation Deck, Huiyang District, 
Huizhou, Guangdong Province 
Ground-side video receiving site: Bijia Lover's Bay, Huidong County

What was evaluated and what was not recorded 
 
Objective 
Evaluate the practical long-range video transmission performance of the supplied 5.8 GHz wireless link at two field 
distances and compare directional and omni antenna behavior at the longer route. 
Evaluation points 
• Link establishment and end -to-end video availability at 3.86 km and 9.78 km.  
• Observed video smoothness under the tested antenna and bitrate combinations.  
• Instantaneous runtime indicators captured from the device web interface.  
• Suitability of directional versus omni antennas for the tested long -range use case.

08 ENGINEERING INTERPRETATION  
Clearly separated from the source-derived observations 
 
Interpretation of the 9.78 km results 
• The directional antenna result indicates that additional antenna gain and focused energy materially improve the link margin a t 
the longest tested distance.  
• The omni antenna remaining smooth at 512 kbps but showing minor stuttering at 1024 kbps is consistent with a reduced fade 
margin: a higher application bitrate leaves less tolerance for retransmissions and latency variation.  
• The -94 dBm / 12% screenshot represents a weak -link state. The visible ping variation up to approximately 206 ms is
